name: UKRAINE

flag.title: Blue & Yellow
flag.note: Blue sky over golden wheat fields

lead: Ukraine has golden wheat fields under wide blue skies. Its flag has those same two colours. Golden-domed churches shine in Kyiv, the capital. Ukrainians paint eggs, sew embroidered shirts.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Ukraine is the largest country wholly inside Europe. It is bigger than France. Most of it is flat, fertile steppe (grassland).
In the south, the Black Sea has sandy beaches. In the west, the green Carpathian Mountains rise to Hoverla, the highest peak.
animals: Przewalski’s horse is the last wild horse on Earth. It roams the Chornobyl zone, empty since a nuclear accident. Pink pelicans nest in the Danube Delta, where a river meets the sea.
The steppe eagle hunts ground squirrels. Wolves, lynx, and European bison live in the forests. Catfish as long as a car swim in the Dnipro River.
culture: Ukrainians paint pysanky, Easter eggs with tiny wax-and-dye patterns. Each symbol has a meaning. Spirals mean forever. Wheat means a good harvest.
People wear embroidered vyshyvanka shirts at festivals and school. Borshch is a deep-red beetroot soup. UNESCO (a UN culture group) lists it as living culture.
history: Over 1,000 years ago, Kyiv led a powerful realm called Kyivan Rus. It was one of medieval Europe’s greatest states. Saint Sophia Cathedral was built around 1037 AD and still stands.

For centuries, the Polish, Russian, and Ottoman (Turkish) empires split Ukraine. Cossack warriors on horseback fought for freedom. Ukraine became fully independent in 1991, when the Soviet Union (a huge state led by Russia) collapsed.
wows: Ukraine supplies about a third of the world’s sunflower oil, more than any other country.
In 1710, Cossack leader Pylyp Orlyk wrote one of the world’s first democratic constitutions (rule books).
Kyiv’s Arsenalna metro station is 105 m underground, deeper than London’s Big Ben clock tower is tall.
The empty Chornobyl zone is one of Europe’s largest wildlife sanctuaries, where wolves and wild horses thrive.
The Carpathians hold over 70% of Europe’s ancient beech forest.
Viking-age Kyiv ruins held game pieces carved from bone and walrus tusk.
Ukraine has Europe’s largest titanium (a strong, light metal) reserves.

myths.fact: Its name is just Ukraine, with no “the”. Many Ukrainians dislike the old-fashioned “the”.

myths.myth: Sunflowers follow the sun all day
myths.fact: Only young sunflowers turn with the sun. Grown-up flowers stop and face east.
